# Required package.xml fields

This page is for developers who write or edit the `package.xml` of a site package by hand. It lists what the code
**refuses** a package without, and why, so a package does not fail on the first install that uses it. The meaning
of every element is in [The package.xml reference](../basics/package-xml-reference.md); this page is only about what
must be there and in what form.

## What every import checks

Every way of importing a package goes through `eZPackage::import()` in `kernel/classes/ezpackage.php`: the setup
wizard's download and upload, `php ezpm.php import`, and `package/upload` in the administration. It reads the
definition and stops when:

| Problem | Result |
|---|---|
| No `package.xml` or `package.json` as a plain file at the top of the archive | The definition cannot be read, the import fails |
| No `<name>`, or an empty one | "A package definition without a name was not read" in the debug log |
| A version, release or type that is not a plain token | "A package definition with an invalid version / release / type was not read" |
| A name the `identifier` transformation would change | `STATUS_INVALID_NAME`: "The package name ... is invalid, cannot import the package" |
| A package of that name is already imported | `STATUS_ALREADY_EXISTS`: "Package ... already exists, cannot import the package" |
| The vendor gives no usable directory name | "The package ... names no usable repository, not imported" |

The upload page in the administration checks more, before anything is extracted
(`eZPackageUploadInspector::definition()`); see [The ezpublish and packaging elements](#the-ezpublish-and-packaging-elements).

## The name

**Enforced.** `eZPackage::isValidName()` runs the name through the `identifier` transformation of
`settings/transform.ini` and accepts it only when nothing changes. The transformation ends in `lowercase` and
`identifier_cleanup` (`lib/ezi18n/classes/ezcodemapper.php`), so a valid name:

- has only the characters `a` to `z`, `0` to `9` and `_`;
- has no upper case letter, space, hyphen or dot;
- does not start or end with `_`, and has no `__`.

| Name | Valid | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `sevenx_multisite` | yes | |
| `cjw_multisite_democontent` | yes | |
| `MySite` | no | upper case |
| `my-site` | no | hyphen |
| `my_site_` | no | trailing `_` |

The administration upload also applies `eZPackageRequestGuard::isSafeName()`, which limits the name to 200
characters. The package creation wizard refuses an invalid name with "it can only contain characters in the range
a-z, 0-9 and underscore" (`kernel/classes/ezpackagecreationhandler.php`).

> **Tip**
> Names are global on an installation: an import is refused when any repository already holds a package of that
> name. Prefix your packages with your own short name (as `sevenx_` and `cjw_` do) rather than reusing a shipped
> name.

## Version, release and type

**Enforced.** Since the review of 15 October 2026, `eZPackage::parseDOMTree()` refuses a definition whose
`<version><number>`, `<version><release>` or `<type value="...">` is not a plain token
(`eZPackage::isValidDefinitionToken()`): empty, or 1 to 64 characters from `0-9 A-Z a-z . _ + -`. White space
around the value is trimmed first.

| Value | Accepted |
|---|---|
| `6.0` | yes |
| `15-stable` | yes |
| `1.0.0-beta.1+20261018` | yes |
| `6.0 final` | no, space |
| `<b>1.0</b>` | no, markup |

What the version should look like is on [Version numbers](version-numbers.md). For a site package the type must
also be exactly `site`, or the setup wizard does not list it ([Package types](../basics/package-types.md)).

## The vendor

**Enforced.** `<vendor>` becomes the repository directory under `var/storage/packages/`, after the `urlalias`
transformation; without a vendor the package goes to `local`. A vendor that leaves no usable directory name (for
example `..`) is refused. The shipped packages all say `<vendor>7x</vendor>`, the value of
`[RepositorySettings] Vendor` in `settings/package.ini`, and so land in `var/storage/packages/7x/`.

## The ezpublish and packaging elements

**Enforced on `package/upload`.** The upload inspector refuses a definition that has no `<ezpublish>` element or no
`<packaging>` element with the message "The package.xml of the archive lacks its version or packaging information"
(`definition_incomplete`). It also refuses a root element other than `<package>` and any DOCTYPE. The setup
wizard's own download does not run this check, so a package without them can install through the wizard and still
be refused by the upload page.

```xml
<ezpublish>
  <version>6.0.15-stable</version>
  <named-version>6.0</named-version>
</ezpublish>
<packaging>
  <timestamp>1705211779</timestamp>
  <host>packages.example.com</host>
</packaging>
```

`<ezpublish>` is the name the format has always used for the product version; Exponential keeps it as it is.

## What is not checked

These are read and shown, but nothing refuses a package for lacking them. All of them are conventions of the
shipped packages:

| Element | Shipped 7x packages | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `<summary>` | always | Package list, package page, setup wizard |
| `<description>` | always | Package page, setup wizard |
| `install_type` attribute | `import` for site and site style packages, `install` for the others | Package page ("Imported" or "Install") |
| `<licence>`, `<state>` | `GPL`, `stable` | Package page |
| `<maintainers>` | 15 of 16 | Package page |

The `version` and `is_active` attributes on `<package>` (the shipped packages write `version="6.0.15-0"` or
`version="3.5.2"`) are not read by `parseDOMTree()`. When the kernel writes a package it puts the format version
`3.5.2` (`eZPackage::VERSION`) there.

## A minimal definition that passes

This passes every check above, including the upload page. It is the floor, not the recommendation: the shipped
packages carry everything listed under [What is not checked](#what-is-not-checked) as well.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<package version="3.5.2" development="false" install_type="import">
  <name>example_site</name>
  <summary>Example site</summary>
  <vendor>example</vendor>
  <type value="site" />
  <ezpublish>
    <version>6.0.15-stable</version>
    <named-version>6.0</named-version>
  </ezpublish>
  <packaging>
    <timestamp>1791331200</timestamp>
    <host>packages.example.com</host>
  </packaging>
  <version>
    <number>1.0.0</number>
    <release>1</release>
  </version>
</package>
```
